title: Conjecture 1.3
statement_text: For any $d \geq 3$ and any fixed $k$, the set of all limit points of the vectors $(\lambda_1(G_i), \lambda_2(G_i), \ldots, \lambda_k(G_i))$ for an infinite sequence $G_i$ of $d$-regular graphs is exactly the set $$B(d,k) = \{(\mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots, \mu_k) : d = \mu_1 \geq \mu_2 \geq \mu_3 \geq \ldots \geq \mu_k \geq 2\sqrt{d-1}\}.$$
context_text: For a graph $G$ on $n$ vertices, $\lambda_1(G)\ge\lambda_2(G)\ge\dots\ge\lambda_n(G)$ are the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix; for $d$-regular $G$, $\lambda_1(G)=d$, and the Alon–Boppana bound gives $\lambda_2(G)\ge(1-o(1))2\sqrt{d-1}$. Answering a question of Sarnak, the authors prove that for every $d\ge3$ the set of limit points of $\lambda_2(G_i)$ over infinite sequences of $d$-regular graphs $G_i$ is exactly $[2\sqrt{d-1},d]$, i.e. the case $k=2$ of this conjecture. The inclusion of the set of limit points in $B(d,k)$ follows from the known fact that for fixed $d$ and $k$, every sufficiently large $d$-regular graph has at least $k$ eigenvalues at least $2\sqrt{d-1}-o(1)$; the authors could not decide whether every point of $B(d,k)$ is a limit point even for $k=3$. They prove that every point of $B(d,k)$ with $\mu_k\ge2\sqrt{d-1}+1/\sqrt{d-1}$ is a limit point of $d$-regular graphs, and that every point of $B(d,k)$ is a limit point if the graphs are only required to have maximum degree at most $d$.
paper_title: The limit points of the top and bottom eigenvalues of regular graphs
